questions.question: A triangle is described only in words: its three sides measure 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm, and its three angles measure 37 degrees, 53 degrees and 90 degrees. The page has been turned so the square corner points down and to the right instead of sitting at the bottom left. Using only these numbers, how is the triangle classified by sides and by angles?
options: Scalene acute triangle, because once the square corner is turned it stops being a right angle
questions.explain: Three different side lengths (3 cm, 4 cm, 5 cm) means scalene, and a 90 degree angle means right, so it is a scalene right triangle. The common trap is thinking a turned page changes the angle — 90 degrees stays 90 degrees no matter which way the corner points.

questions.question: A triangle is described only in words: all three of its sides measure 6 cm, and each of its three angles measures 60 degrees. It is drawn tilted on the page, so not one of its sides is horizontal. How is this triangle classified by sides and by angles?
options: Isosceles acute triangle, because tilting it makes the sides stop being equal
questions.explain: All three sides equal means equilateral, and all three angles under 90 degrees means acute. The trap is letting a tilt fool you: a 6 cm side is still 6 cm whichever direction it points.

questions.question: A triangle is described only in words: two of its sides are 5 cm each and the third side is 8 cm; its angles measure 36 degrees, 36 degrees and 108 degrees. It is drawn upside down, with the 8 cm side across the top and the 108 degree corner at the bottom. How is it classified by sides and by angles?
options: Isosceles acute triangle, because the wide corner only looks obtuse when the triangle is upside down
questions.explain: Exactly two equal sides (5 cm and 5 cm) means isosceles, and one angle bigger than 90 degrees (108 degrees) means obtuse. Flipping the triangle upside down does not shrink that 108 degree corner.

questions.question: A triangle is described only in words: two of its sides are 5 cm each and the third side is longer than both of them; its angles measure 45 degrees, 45 degrees and 90 degrees. It is drawn resting on its longest side, so the square corner points straight up at the ceiling. How is it classified by sides and by angles?
options: Isosceles acute triangle, because a right angle only counts when it sits at a bottom corner
questions.explain: Two equal sides means isosceles, and the 90 degree angle means right, so it is an isosceles right triangle. The trap is thinking a square corner must sit at the bottom — a right angle is a right angle pointing up, down or sideways.

questions.question: In triangle PQR, angle P measures 25 degrees and angle Q measures 130 degrees. The triangle is drawn with the 130 degree corner near the bottom of the page. Classify triangle PQR by sides and by angles.
options: Isosceles acute triangle, because the 130 degree corner points downward so it opens the other way
questions.explain: First find angle R: 180 - 25 - 130 = 25 degrees, so two angles match and the triangle is isosceles; the 130 degree angle makes it obtuse. The trap is thinking a corner that points downward opens differently — the measure never changes with direction.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, angle A measures 60 degrees and angle B measures 60 degrees. The triangle is drawn point-down, with one side across the top. Classify triangle ABC by sides and by angles.
options: Equilateral acute when it is point-up, but isosceles acute when it is point-down
questions.explain: The third angle is 180 - 60 - 60 = 60 degrees, so all three angles are equal, which means all three sides are equal: equilateral, and all angles under 90 degrees means acute. The trap is thinking flipping it point-down changes the type — the same three 60 degree angles are still there.

questions.question: A sail at Kits Beach is shaped like a triangle. Two of its angles measure 55 degrees each, and the third measures 70 degrees. The sail hangs so that the 70 degree corner is at the bottom. Classify the sail by sides and by angles.
options: Scalene acute triangle, because you can never tell that sides match without measuring them
Isosceles obtuse triangle, because the 70 degree corner points downward and downward corners are wide
questions.explain: Two equal angles (55 degrees and 55 degrees) sit across from two equal sides, so the sail is isosceles, and since 55, 55 and 70 are all under 90 degrees it is acute. The trap is judging a corner by which way it points instead of by its measure.

questions.question: A triangle has angles measuring 90 degrees, 45 degrees and 45 degrees. Which statement about this triangle is true no matter how it is turned on the page?
options: It is isosceles and right only while the square corner sits at the bottom; once it is turned it becomes isosceles and acute
questions.explain: Two equal angles mean two equal sides, so it is isosceles, and the 90 degree angle makes it right. Turning a shape is a rotation: every side length and every angle measure stays exactly the same, so the classification cannot change.

questions.question: A playground in Surrey has two identical triangular climbing panels, each with sides of 2 m, 2 m and 2 m. One panel is bolted on point-up and the other is bolted on point-down. Jae says, “The point-up one is equilateral, but the point-down one is only isosceles.” Which reply is correct?
options: Jae is wrong, because both panels are equilateral and acute — turning a shape never changes its sides or its angles
Jae is right, because the side that moves to the top gets stretched longer, leaving that panel with only two equal sides
Jae is wrong, because both panels are isosceles but neither one is equilateral, since equal sides make a triangle isosceles
Jae is right, because a triangle sitting point-down can only be isosceles, since its wide top side becomes a different base
questions.explain: Both panels have three 2 m sides, so both are equilateral, and every equilateral triangle has three 60 degree angles, so both are acute. The trap is believing a flip changes the shape — bolting a panel point-down moves it but does not resize a single side.

questions.question: Ravi is sorting triangle tiles for a quilt. Tile A has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 5 cm. Tile B has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm, with angles of 37 degrees, 37 degrees and 106 degrees. Tile C has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm with one 90 degree angle, and it is glued down upside down. Ravi must place every right triangle in one pile. Which tiles belong in the right-triangle pile?
options: No tiles, because Tile C is upside down so its square corner does not count
questions.explain: Check each tile for a 90 degree angle: Tile A is equilateral with three 60 degree angles, Tile B has a 106 degree angle so it is obtuse, and only Tile C has a 90 degree angle, making it the scalene right tile. The trap is letting the upside-down gluing cancel a right angle — position never changes an angle measure.

questions.question: Ellie draws a triangle and measures its angles: 90 degrees, 60 degrees and 30 degrees, with all three sides different lengths. She then rotates her page a quarter turn and measures again, getting the same three angles. Her partner Sam says the triangle turned into an obtuse triangle because its longest side now runs across the top. Who is right, and why?
options: Sam is right, because angles should always be measured from the bottom edge of the page
Sam is right, because the corner that looks widest on the page is the obtuse one
Ellie is right, because the angles still measure 90, 60 and 30 degrees, so it is still a scalene right triangle
Ellie is right about the angles, but the triangle is now isosceles right because two of its sides look the same length
questions.explain: Classify from the measures, not the picture: three different sides means scalene and a 90 degree angle means right, and rotating the page changed neither. The trap is judging by how a corner or side looks after a turn instead of by the numbers you measured.

questions.question: A triangular garden plot at a community garden in Victoria is fenced with sections of 9 m, 9 m and 14 m. The corner between the two 9 m sections measures 102 degrees. The gardener rotates the plan on the table so that the 102 degree corner ends up at the top left instead of the bottom. Which classification and reason are both correct?
options: Isosceles acute, because the other two angles are 39 degrees each, and two acute angles out of three make the triangle acute
Scalene obtuse, because after the plan is rotated the two 9 m sections no longer match, though the 102 degree corner stays obtuse
Isosceles right, because a 102 degree corner is close enough to a square corner, and the two 9 m sides are the equal pair
Isosceles obtuse, because two sides are 9 m and one angle is greater than 90 degrees, and rotating the plan changes neither
questions.explain: Two sides of 9 m make it isosceles, and the 102 degree angle is greater than 90 degrees so it is obtuse — the other two angles work out to 39 degrees each, but one obtuse angle is enough to make the whole triangle obtuse. Two traps here: rounding 102 degrees down to a right angle, and thinking a rotated plan un-matches the two equal fence sections.
